launch-tn-nashville-centennial-park.summary: Nashville's 132-acre signature urban park, centered on the full-scale Parthenon with Lake Watauga, gardens, monuments, arts facilities, events, trails, dog areas, volleyball, and the adjacent Sportsplex.
launch-tn-nashville-centennial-park.hours: Open daily from dawn to 11:00 p.m. The Parthenon, Sportsplex, Arts Center, dog park, concessions, programs, and events use separate schedules.
launch-tn-nashville-centennial-park.parking: Use an open lot nearest the Parthenon, Arts Center, Sportsplex, or dog park. Phase-three work closes the north side and part of 27th Avenue through fall 2026; Parthenon and Arts Center lots remain accessible.
launch-tn-nashville-centennial-park.arrival: This is a multi-destination park. Route to the Parthenon for the landmark and museum, 25th Avenue for Sportsplex access, Flag Pole Hill for dog areas, or the Arts Center for classes and galleries.
launch-tn-nashville-centennial-park.restrooms: Restrooms are most dependable inside staffed destinations such as the Parthenon, Sportsplex, and Arts Center during their own hours; event facilities and construction can change the closest option.
launch-tn-nashville-centennial-park.cost: Outdoor park, trail, lake, gardens, monuments, lawns, and dog areas are free. Museum admission, Sportsplex use, programs, reservations, food, and ticketed events cost separately.
launch-tn-nashville-centennial-park.accessibility: Major destinations and much of the one-mile loop use paved routes, but current construction, event layouts, grades, lawn surfaces, and temporary detours affect individual approaches.
launch-tn-nashville-centennial-park.dogs: Leash dogs in ordinary park areas. Flag Pole Hill provides separate fenced large- and small-dog areas open dawn to dusk; dogs are restricted from posted buildings and event areas.
launch-tn-nashville-centennial-park.family: Families can explore the Parthenon, gardens, lake loop, monuments, arts programs, and events. The park does not advertise a destination playground or splash pad; Centennial Sportsplex pools are separate and paid.
launch-tn-nashville-centennial-park.transit: WeGo Route 3 runs along West End Avenue from downtown. Choose the stop closest to the Parthenon, Sportsplex, or event and verify live service during festivals.
launch-tn-nashville-centennial-park.need: The north side is under construction through fall 2026. Check current parking, lake-loop detours, event closures, Parthenon admission, Sportsplex schedules, and Metro Parks alerts before a feature-specific trip.

launch-tn-nashville-shelby-bottoms-and-s.summary: A major East Nashville complex combining Shelby Park recreation with a 960-acre Cumberland River floodplain, accessible greenway, primitive trails, wetlands, Nature Center, nature play, lake, golf, playgrounds, and Cornelia Fort Airpark.
launch-tn-nashville-shelby-bottoms-and-s.hours: Shelby Bottoms Greenway is open dawn to dusk daily; Shelby Park is open dawn to 11:00 p.m. The Nature Center has shorter weekday and Saturday hours and is closed Sunday and Monday.
launch-tn-nashville-shelby-bottoms-and-s.parking: Use 1900 Davidson Street for the Nature Center and main greenway trailhead. Park nearer Sevier Lake, playground, community center, golf, Cornelia Fort, or the pedestrian bridge for those distinct destinations.
launch-tn-nashville-shelby-bottoms-and-s.arrival: Start at the Nature Center for maps, exhibits, nature play, and the main greenway. Shelby Park recreation and Cornelia Fort Airpark are separate arrival zones across a very large combined property.
launch-tn-nashville-shelby-bottoms-and-s.restrooms: The Nature Center is the most dependable greenway restroom during its posted hours. Shelby Park facilities serve developed recreation areas, but do not expect restrooms along every trail segment.
launch-tn-nashville-shelby-bottoms-and-s.cost: Nature Center admission, greenway, nature play, and ordinary park access are free. Golf, rentals, permits, community-center activities, shelters, and selected programs cost separately.
launch-tn-nashville-shelby-bottoms-and-s.accessibility: More than five miles of paved greenway provide accessible travel, while primitive paths, wetlands, boardwalks, flood debris, and natural surfaces vary.
launch-tn-nashville-shelby-bottoms-and-s.dogs: Pets are allowed on a leash six feet or shorter. Bikes belong on paved trails only, and collecting natural or historic material requires authorization.
launch-tn-nashville-shelby-bottoms-and-s.family: Nature Play, the Nature Center, paved biking, playgrounds, lake views, Cornelia Fort's broad pavement, and picnics offer varied family choices; waterways are not supervised swimming areas.
launch-tn-nashville-shelby-bottoms-and-s.transit: WeGo routes serve the East Nashville area, but the correct stop depends on the Nature Center, Shelby Park recreation, or Cornelia Fort destination. Verify the final walking route.
launch-tn-nashville-shelby-bottoms-and-s.need: This is Cumberland River floodplain. Check high water, heat, boardwalk or bridge repairs, Nature Center hours, greenway closures, and trail conditions before leaving.
launch-tn-nashville-shelby-bottoms-and-s.dogsNote: Leashed dogs are welcome; keep them out of posted habitat, play, golf, and facility areas.

launch-tn-nashville-warner-parks.summary: Percy and Edwin Warner Parks form a 3,100-acre forest-and-field system with primitive and paved trails, scenic drives, overlooks, Nature Center, nature play, dog park, mountain biking, golf, equestrian facilities, shelters, and athletic areas.
launch-tn-nashville-warner-parks.hours: Parks are open daily from dawn to 11:00 p.m. The Nature Center is open Tuesday-Saturday 9:00 a.m.-4:00 p.m. and closed Sunday and Monday; other facilities differ.
launch-tn-nashville-warner-parks.parking: Use the Nature Center for maps and Edwin Warner trails, Deep Well for Warner Woods and Mossy Ridge, or the exact lot for dog park, golf, equestrian, fields, shelters, and scenic destinations.
launch-tn-nashville-warner-parks.arrival: First-time visitors should start at the Nature Center. The system is too large for one useful central pin, so select a named trailhead or facility before driving.
launch-tn-nashville-warner-parks.restrooms: Restrooms cluster near the Nature Center and selected developed recreation or picnic areas, not throughout primitive trail loops.
launch-tn-nashville-warner-parks.cost: General park, trails, Nature Center, dog park, and ordinary picnics are free. Golf, equestrian services, reservations, permits, and some events cost separately.
launch-tn-nashville-warner-parks.accessibility: Nature Center grounds and paved multi-use routes offer accessible choices; primitive trails are rooted, hilly, muddy, and sometimes crossed by drainage.
launch-tn-nashville-warner-parks.dogs: Leash dogs in ordinary areas and use the fenced dog park for off-leash activity. Pets are prohibited in Burch Reserve and on posted horse-and-pedestrian routes.
launch-tn-nashville-warner-parks.family: Nature Play, Little Acorn, Hungry Hawk, the Nature Center, paved routes, picnics, and wildlife observation are strong family options; there is no managed swim or splash area.
launch-tn-nashville-warner-parks.transit: No single direct transit stop serves this 3,100-acre system. Check WeGo for 7311 Highway 100 and verify that the final walking route is safe and practical.
launch-tn-nashville-warner-parks.need: Download maps before entering because service can be limited. Check storm damage, flooding, downed trees, trail events, heat, ticks, facility hours, and current closures.

launch-tn-nashville-bicentennial-capitol.summary: A free 19-acre downtown state park interpreting Tennessee through a giant map, history path, fountains, carillon, amphitheater, memorials, Capitol views, and direct access to the Nashville Farmers Market.
launch-tn-nashville-bicentennial-capitol.hours: Outdoor park access is generally available daily during posted state-park hours; fountains, carillon programming, tours, market vendors, events, and restrooms use separate schedules.
launch-tn-nashville-bicentennial-capitol.parking: Limited park and street parking competes with Farmers Market, Capitol, museum, and event traffic. Use the exact destination, consider paid downtown parking, and never assume event-day spaces.
launch-tn-nashville-bicentennial-capitol.arrival: Approach from Harrison Street for the map, fountains, and Farmers Market, or from James Robertson Parkway for the Capitol-facing end and carillon.
launch-tn-nashville-bicentennial-capitol.restrooms: Restrooms are associated with staffed park facilities and the adjacent Farmers Market during their schedules; the long outdoor mall itself does not guarantee an open facility at every hour.
launch-tn-nashville-bicentennial-capitol.cost: General park monuments, map, history walk, fountains when operating, lawns, and ordinary programs are free. Food, parking, private events, and selected programs cost.
launch-tn-nashville-bicentennial-capitol.accessibility: The central mall uses broad paved and level routes, though fountain spray, event barricades, crowds, curb approaches, and heat exposure can affect travel.
launch-tn-nashville-bicentennial-capitol.dogs: Leashed dogs may use ordinary outdoor areas under posted rules; keep them out of fountains, memorial surfaces, buildings, food areas, and crowded events.
launch-tn-nashville-bicentennial-capitol.family: The walkable Tennessee map, fountains, bells, history markers, lawns, and Farmers Market make a useful downtown family stop; supervise closely near roads and water jets.
launch-tn-nashville-bicentennial-capitol.transit: Downtown WeGo service and Music City Central are nearby. Walking from the Capitol, Tennessee State Museum, or Farmers Market is often easier than moving a car.
launch-tn-nashville-bicentennial-capitol.need: The park is highly exposed to heat, storms, and event changes. Confirm fountain operation, tours, carillon programs, Farmers Market hours, road closures, and current state-park notices.

launch-tn-nashville-wasioto-park.summary: The downtown east-bank riverfront park formerly called Cumberland Park, with imaginative climbing and nature play, splash features, amphitheater, lawn, trails, skyline views, and Shelby Street Pedestrian Bridge access.
launch-tn-nashville-wasioto-park.hours: Open daily from dawn to 11:00 p.m. Spray-ground operation is seasonal and maintenance dependent; events, elevator access, and reservable spaces can differ.
launch-tn-nashville-wasioto-park.parking: Use designated riverfront or event parking and expect limited availability during stadium events. The park is also reached on foot from downtown across the Shelby Street Pedestrian Bridge.
launch-tn-nashville-wasioto-park.arrival: Route to 592 South First Street for the park, or walk from downtown over the pedestrian bridge. The bridge elevator and stair arrive above the play and event areas.
launch-tn-nashville-wasioto-park.restrooms: Restroom availability is limited and can depend on events or nearby open facilities. Locate an option before settling into the play area with children.
launch-tn-nashville-wasioto-park.cost: Park, playground, trails, skyline views, and spray ground when operating are free. Parking, food, reservations, stadium events, and special programs cost separately.
launch-tn-nashville-wasioto-park.accessibility: Paved routes serve the amphitheater, lawn, and many play areas; bridge elevator outages, steep bridge approaches, water-play surfaces, and crowds can affect access.
launch-tn-nashville-wasioto-park.dogs: Leash dogs and keep them out of splash jets, play equipment, food areas, private events, and posted river-edge spaces.
launch-tn-nashville-wasioto-park.family: The Hollow, Scoops, Gorge, Explorer Trail, slides, climbing nets, sand, and seasonal water features make this a flagship downtown family park.
launch-tn-nashville-wasioto-park.transit: Walk from downtown across the Shelby Street Pedestrian Bridge or use nearby downtown transit and rideshare. Stadium traffic can alter drop-off access.
launch-tn-nashville-wasioto-park.need: The park was renamed from Cumberland Park in 2024. The spray ground has required extensive repairs and the bridge elevator may close for renovation; verify both before promising water play or step-free bridge access.

launch-tn-nashville-radnor-lake-state-na.summary: A protected 1,200-acre natural area eight miles from downtown with lake views, forested ridge trails, wildlife observation, ranger programs, a visitor center, and aviary education facilities.
launch-tn-nashville-radnor-lake-state-na.hours: Natural-area gates and trails follow posted daylight-based hours. The visitor center, aviary, ranger programs, and road access use shorter schedules and can close independently.
launch-tn-nashville-radnor-lake-state-na.parking: Parking is limited at both Otter Creek Road ends and fills early on pleasant weekends. Do not park illegally on shoulders or block gates; arrive early or choose another time.
launch-tn-nashville-radnor-lake-state-na.arrival: Choose the west side for the visitor center and many trail connections or the east side for alternate lake and ridge access. Otter Creek Road through the natural area is reserved for pedestrians during normal operation.
launch-tn-nashville-radnor-lake-state-na.restrooms: The most dependable restrooms are near staffed visitor facilities during posted hours; ridge and lake trails have no facilities.
launch-tn-nashville-radnor-lake-state-na.cost: General natural-area access, trails, wildlife viewing, and many ranger programs are free; donations and selected programs may apply.
launch-tn-nashville-radnor-lake-state-na.accessibility: Visitor facilities and portions of Otter Creek Road offer smoother access, but natural trails include roots, rocks, stairs, steep grades, mud, and narrow sections.
launch-tn-nashville-radnor-lake-state-na.dogs: Pets are not allowed on Radnor Lake trails or in the natural area except qualifying service animals. Choose a different park for dog walking.
launch-tn-nashville-radnor-lake-state-na.family: Short lake views, wildlife, ranger programs, and the aviary can work well for prepared families. Trails are not playgrounds; keep children quiet, close, hydrated, and on route.
launch-tn-nashville-radnor-lake-state-na.transit: Direct public transit is limited. Verify the complete final approach before relying on transit or rideshare, and arrange a pickup where service is dependable.
launch-tn-nashville-radnor-lake-state-na.need: This is a wildlife sanctuary, not a general recreation park: no jogging, biking, pets, picnicking, fishing, boating, or leaving marked routes. Check parking, weather, trail closures, and visitor-center hours.

launch-tn-nashville-fort-negley-park.summary: A free historic landscape two miles from Lower Broadway interpreting Union-occupied Nashville, the African American laborers who built the fort, Civil War history, WPA reconstruction, archaeology, and skyline views.
launch-tn-nashville-fort-negley-park.hours: Park open dawn to dusk. Visitor Center: Tuesday-Friday noon-4:00 p.m. and Saturday 9:00 a.m.-4:00 p.m.; closed Sunday and Monday.
launch-tn-nashville-fort-negley-park.parking: Parking is very limited during the 2026 master-plan construction. Carpool when possible and follow temporary signs for the active entrance and work zones.
launch-tn-nashville-fort-negley-park.arrival: Use the Visitor Center for exhibits, films, maps, restrooms, and current construction guidance. The half-mile park trail remains open, but hilltop fort access is temporarily closed.
launch-tn-nashville-fort-negley-park.restrooms: Restrooms are available inside the Visitor Center only during its posted hours; the outdoor park remains open when the building is closed.
launch-tn-nashville-fort-negley-park.cost: Park trail, overlooks, outdoor interpretation, Visitor Center exhibits, and films are free. Special programs or private events may differ.
launch-tn-nashville-fort-negley-park.accessibility: Paved interpretive routes were designed for broad access, but active construction, hill grades, temporary entrances, and the closed fort structure affect the current visit.
launch-tn-nashville-fort-negley-park.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome on open outdoor paths. Keep pets out of the Visitor Center, construction zones, fragile stonework, and posted restricted areas.
launch-tn-nashville-fort-negley-park.family: The short trail, skyline view, exhibits, 20-minute film, and outdoor panels can support a focused history visit; supervise around grades, work vehicles, and historic masonry.
launch-tn-nashville-fort-negley-park.transit: The site is near downtown but separated by major roads and grades. Verify WeGo, walking, or rideshare routing to the current entrance rather than navigating only to the old stadium lot.
launch-tn-nashville-fort-negley-park.need: Phase-one construction is active in 2026. The half-mile trail and Visitor Center remain open, but access to the historic hilltop fort is closed until the announced reopening; check current notices before visiting.

launch-tn-nashville-two-rivers-park.summary: A 374-acre Donelson recreation hub connecting Wave Country, golf, mansion grounds, skate and disc golf, dog park, shelters, athletic space, and the Stones River Greenway across the Cumberland pedestrian bridge.
launch-tn-nashville-two-rivers-park.hours: Open daily from dawn to 11:00 p.m. Wave Country, golf, mansion tours, dog park, facilities, rentals, and events use separate or seasonal schedules.
launch-tn-nashville-two-rivers-park.parking: Choose the lot for the exact destination. Wave Country, mansion, golf, skatepark, dog park, shelters, and greenway trailheads are spread across the 374-acre property.
launch-tn-nashville-two-rivers-park.arrival: McGavock Pike serves the main park, while greenway users may arrive from Shelby Bottoms across the Cumberland River pedestrian bridge. Do not use one broad pin for every activity.
launch-tn-nashville-two-rivers-park.restrooms: Restrooms are tied to staffed or developed facilities such as Wave Country, golf, mansion events, and selected recreation areas; trail access alone does not guarantee one is open.
launch-tn-nashville-two-rivers-park.cost: Ordinary park, greenway, skatepark, disc golf, dog park, and picnic access are free. Wave Country, golf, mansion programs, rentals, reservations, and events cost separately.
launch-tn-nashville-two-rivers-park.accessibility: Paved greenway and developed facilities provide accessible options, but bridge grades, golf boundaries, field surfaces, construction, and seasonal operations vary.
launch-tn-nashville-two-rivers-park.dogs: Leash dogs in ordinary park areas and use the designated dog park for off-leash activity. Pets are restricted from Wave Country, golf play, buildings, and posted events.
launch-tn-nashville-two-rivers-park.family: Wave Country's paid seasonal pools and slides, skatepark, disc golf, mansion grounds, greenway, shelters, and dog park provide varied family outings.
launch-tn-nashville-two-rivers-park.transit: Driving, rideshare, biking, and the connected greenway are practical options. Confirm WeGo service and the final walk to the specific facility.
launch-tn-nashville-two-rivers-park.need: This is Nashville's most facility-diverse park. Verify Wave Country season and admission, golf or mansion schedules, greenway closures, bridge conditions, event traffic, and the exact parking zone.
